## About

**UDPTagger** is a browser-based part-of-speech tagging and dependency parsing tool developed by the [Language Technology and Data Analysis Laboratory (LADAL)](https://ladal.edu.au) at the University of Queensland. It uses the [UDPipe](https://ufal.mff.cuni.cz/udpipe) toolkit to tokenise, lemmatise, POS-tag, and dependency-parse plain-text files in over 65 languages — with no R knowledge or software installation required.

Results are available in two formats: a **tidy annotation table** (one row per token) and **annotated text files** (word_UPOSTAG format), both downloadable immediately after tagging.

::: {.callout-note}
This tool accompanies the LADAL tutorial [**Part-of-Speech Tagging and Dependency Parsing with R**](https://ladal.edu.au/tutorials/postag/postag.html), which explains the methodology in depth and provides reusable R code for more advanced workflows.
:::

---

## What does UDPTagger do?

For each uploaded text, UDPTagger performs four annotation steps in a single pass:

**Tokenisation** — splits the text into individual tokens (words and punctuation marks), handling language-specific conventions such as clitics, contractions, and punctuation attachment.

**Lemmatisation** — reduces each token to its canonical dictionary form (e.g. *running* → *run*, *better* → *good*).

**Part-of-speech tagging** — assigns each token two POS labels: a **UPOS** (Universal POS tag, consistent across all languages) and an **XPOS** (language-specific tag from the treebank's own tagset).

**Dependency parsing** — assigns each token a syntactic head (the token it depends on) and a dependency relation label (e.g. `nsubj`, `obj`, `amod`), producing a full dependency tree for every sentence.

---

## How to use

1. **Launch** the tool using one of the Binder links below.
2. **Upload** one or more `.txt` files — each file becomes one document.
3. **Select a language model** from the dropdown. Models marked **★** are pre-loaded and start instantly. Others download automatically on first use (typically 10–30 seconds).
4. **Click Tag texts.**
5. **Explore** results across four tabs:
   - **Tidy table** — one row per token with all annotation columns; sortable, filterable
   - **POS summary** — bar chart of token counts by UPOS category
   - **Annotated texts** — preview and download of `word_UPOSTAG` format files
   - **Tag guide** — reference table of UPOS tags and dependency relations
6. **Download** results:
   - Tidy table as **Excel** (`.xlsx`) or **CSV**
   - Annotated text files as a **ZIP** archive of `.txt` files

---

## Output formats

### Tidy table

One row per token with the following columns:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `Document` | Source filename (without extension) |
| `Sentence` | Sentence number within document |
| `TokenID` | Token position within sentence |
| `Token` | Surface form (as it appears in the text) |
| `Lemma` | Dictionary/base form |
| `UPOS` | Universal POS tag (consistent across languages) |
| `XPOS` | Language-specific POS tag |
| `DepRel` | Dependency relation to head token |
| `HeadTokenID` | Token ID of the syntactic head |

### Annotated text files

One `.txt` file per uploaded document, named `[original_filename]_postag.txt`. Each token is written as `word_UPOSTAG` with a space between tokens. Sentence boundaries are preserved with a blank line.

Example:
```
The_DET cat_NOUN sat_VERB on_ADP the_DET mat_NOUN ._PUNCT
```

## Language models

UDPTagger provides models for 65+ languages from [Universal Dependencies](https://universaldependencies.org/). Many languages have multiple models trained on different treebanks — choose the model that best matches your text type (e.g. `english-ewt` for general text, `english-gum` for academic/web text).

### Pre-loaded models *(start instantly)*

These models are bundled into the Binder image and require no download:

| Language | Available models |
|---|---|
| Arabic | arabic-padt |
| Chinese | chinese-gsd · chinese-gsdsimp |
| Dutch | dutch-alpino · dutch-lassysmall |
| English | **english-ewt ★** · english-gum · english-lines · english-partut |
| French | french-gsd · french-partut · french-sequoia · french-spoken |
| German | german-gsd · german-hdt |
| Italian | italian-isdt · italian-partut · italian-postwita · italian-twittiro · italian-vit |
| Japanese | japanese-gsd |
| Portuguese | portuguese-bosque · portuguese-br · portuguese-gsd |
| Russian | russian-gsd · russian-syntagrus · russian-taiga |
| Spanish | spanish-ancora · spanish-gsd |

### Download-on-demand

All other languages (Afrikaans, Ancient Greek, Armenian, Basque, Bulgarian, Catalan, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Estonian, Finnish, Galician, Gothic, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Irish, Japanese, Kazakh, Korean, Latin, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, Marathi, Norwegian, Persian, Polish, Romanian, Sanskrit, Serbian, Slovak, Slovenian, Swedish, Tamil, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu, Vietnamese, and more) download automatically when selected — typically in 10–30 seconds.

## Universal POS tags (UPOS)

| Tag | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| NOUN | Common noun | *dog, city, music* |
| VERB | Main verb | *run, eat, think* |
| ADJ | Adjective | *big, old, green* |
| ADV | Adverb | *very, well, exactly* |
| PROPN | Proper noun | *London, Mary, UNESCO* |
| PRON | Pronoun | *I, he, they, who* |
| DET | Determiner | *the, a, this, every* |
| ADP | Adposition | *in, to, during* |
| AUX | Auxiliary verb | *is, will, have* |
| CCONJ | Coordinating conjunction | *and, but, or* |
| SCONJ | Subordinating conjunction | *that, because, if* |
| NUM | Numeral | *1, 2021, one, first* |
| PART | Particle | *not, 's, up* |
| INTJ | Interjection | *oh, well, yes, hmm* |
| PUNCT | Punctuation | *. , ; : ! ?* |
| SYM | Symbol | *%, $, =, ©* |
| X | Other / unknown | foreign words, typos |

Full documentation: [universaldependencies.org/u/pos/](https://universaldependencies.org/u/pos/)

## Launch

::: {.callout-tip}
## Which link should I use?

Use **ARDC BinderHub** if you have an Australian or New Zealand research institution login (AAF or Tuakiri). It offers more computing resources and faster load times.

Use **MyBinder.org** if you do not have AAF/Tuakiri access. It is free and open to everyone.

**Note:** The first launch after a Binder rebuild will be slower than usual (~5–10 minutes) because the pre-bundled models are downloaded during the build. Subsequent launches use the cached image and start in 1–2 minutes.
:::

**ARDC BinderHub** *(recommended — requires AAF / Tuakiri login)*

```
https://binderhub.atap-binder.cloud.edu.au/v2/gh/SLCLADAL/interactive-notebooks-environment/main?urlpath=git-pull%3Frepo%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fgithub.com%252FSLCLADAL%252Ftools%26urlpath%3Dshiny%252Ftree%252Ftools%252Fudptagger%252F%26branch%3Dmain
```

**MyBinder.org** *(open access — no login required)*

```
https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/SLCLADAL/interactive-notebooks-environment/main?urlpath=git-pull%3Frepo%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fgithub.com%252FSLCLADAL%252Ftools%26urlpath%3Dshiny%252Ftree%252Ftools%252Fudptagger%252F%26branch%3Dmain
```

## Input format

UDPTagger accepts **plain-text files only** (`.txt`). Files should be:

- Saved with UTF-8 encoding (the tool converts other encodings automatically where possible)
- Unformatted (no Word `.docx`, no PDF, no HTML)
- One file per document — the filename becomes the `Document` label in the tidy table

---

## Dependencies

All packages are pre-installed in the [LADAL interactive notebooks environment](https://github.com/SLCLADAL/interactive-notebooks-environment):

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `shiny` | Web application framework |
| `udpipe` | Tokenisation, POS tagging, lemmatisation, dependency parsing |
| `zip` | Creating ZIP archives for annotated text download |
| `tidyverse` | Data manipulation and CSV export |
| `writexl` | Excel export |
| `DT` | Interactive annotation table |
| `ggplot2` | POS frequency bar chart |

::: {.callout-important}
## Environment note

`zip` must be added to `install.R` in the
[interactive-notebooks-environment](https://github.com/SLCLADAL/interactive-notebooks-environment)
if not already present. The model pre-download script also needs to run
at build time via a `postBuild` file — see `DEPLOYMENT.md`.
:::
